ONE REAL violin from a published CT study for pexfp.199 (mail 5226). A 1743 del Gesu, NOT the UIowa violin of the recordings, whose own dimensions stay UNKNOWN (u-not-iowa-violin); population-grade stand-in only

CC-BY-4.0 (ESRF DataCite record, issued 2026); attribution: ESRF; data authors Paul Tafforeau, Luigi Paolasini and Alessandro Mirone, segmentation by Paul Tafforeau (the scan metadata file); the record states no licence of the instrument's owner beyond the ESRF's
propagation phase-contrast synchrotron tomography, helical, 12000 projections, 35.66 um voxel, volume 5947 x 3165 x 16933 voxels (the scan metadata file of dataset 2416550332)

measured on the fetched meshes with tools/geometry/violin-cannone-esrf/mesh_resolution.py: the part meshes are decimated copies of the CT surface, not voxel-sized: median edge 0.19 mm for the top plate (5.4 voxels, 90th percentile 0.46 mm), 0.16 mm for the back plate, 0.17 mm for the ribs; the whole-violin STL named 200K holds 3508724 triangles and the one named 10M holds 10027320, so the names are not triangle counts; their volumes differ by 0.06 percent (694157 and 694565 mm3), their areas by 0.4 percent and their sections at z = -100 and -190 mm, y = 5 mm and x = 30 mm by at most 0.09 percent; every part mesh checked is closed (each edge used twice, a few exceptions in the tailpiece) and the STL header states Unit:Millimeter

every length in the data tables is in millimetres in the frame of the source files (frames.tsv); dimensions.tsv is in SI

this lane's numpy-only scripts (tools/geometry/violin-cannone-esrf/): plate outlines, holes and thickness from a 0.5 mm raster of the surface samples of each closed plate mesh (3 mm blocks in the map tables); sections of bar, post, bridge, neck, fingerboard, tail block and strings by planes; rib and lining sections by half-planes through the vertical axis every 2 degrees

the 4 string meshes give equivalent diameters 1.095, 1.094, 0.826 and 0.266 mm and the soundpost 6.35 mm (1/4 inch); the string bridge contacts agree to 0.2 mm in z and the nut contacts of three strings to 0.2 mm; the STL header states Unit:Millimeter
